```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

This article lists the errors and surprises you may meet, what each means, and
what to do. Errors from the package name the function you called and, where it
matters, the argument.

## Credentials

### "CDC Locator API credentials not found"

R can't find your client ID and token, so nothing was sent.

- If you added them to `.Renviron`, restart R: the file is read at startup.
- If the project you're working in has its own `.Renviron`, R reads that file
  instead of the one in your home folder. Add the credentials there too, or
  remove the project's file.
- Check the names are exactly `CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_ID` and
  `CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_TOKEN`.
- Check, without printing the values:

```{r}
nzchar(Sys.getenv(c("CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_ID", "CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_TOKEN")))
```

`vignette("credentials-and-networks")` covers the ways to set them.

### "`client_id` must be a single non-empty string"

`cdc_locator_set_credentials()` got an empty, missing or multi-value argument.
The message names the argument but never shows its value.

### "`install = TRUE` needs an interactive session"

Saving to `.Renviron` asks for confirmation, so it can't run from a script run
with `Rscript`, in a scheduled job or while knitting. Run it once at the
console instead. Nothing was set or saved.

### "has characters that can't be saved safely in .Renviron"

`.Renviron` treats spaces, quotes, `#` and `$` specially, and a line break
would split the line, so `install = TRUE` only saves plain values. Use
`install = FALSE` to set the credentials for this session only, and run it
again in each new session. Nothing was set or saved.

### A warning that "this folder has its own .Renviron"

The credentials were saved to your home `.Renviron`, but the folder R is
running in has its own `.Renviron`. R reads that file instead when it starts
here, so add the two lines to it as well, or remove it.

## HTTP errors from the API

These start with `HTTP` and a status code. When the API sent an explanation,
the error adds it after "The API said:", with your credentials removed.

### HTTP 403 Forbidden

The API refused the request. There are two usual causes, and the error lists
both:

- **The key was refused.** The ID or token is wrong, has expired or has been
  revoked. Check `.Renviron` for typos, extra spaces or quotes, and restart R.
  If it still fails from a network that has worked before, contact HIV.gov.
- **The network was refused.** The API has refused requests from outside the
  US and from some cloud servers, including GitHub Actions runners on
  Microsoft Azure. A VPN can have the same effect.

To tell which, try the same code from a home or office connection in the US.
`vignette("credentials-and-networks")` has more detail.

### HTTP 500 with "The API said: No point found for address"

The API doesn't recognize the ZIP code. The package checks that a ZIP code
has five digits, but it can't know which ZIP codes exist. Check the number,
or use `cdc_address_place()` to look one up from a city and state.

### A warning that ZIP codes were skipped

When you search several ZIP codes, a ZIP code the API doesn't know ("No
point found for address", see the section above) is skipped and the others
carry on. The warning lists the skipped ZIP codes, and
`attr(result, "failures")` has the API's message for each. Any other error,
such as a refused request (HTTP 403) or a gateway error, stops the whole
search instead, since it could affect every ZIP code.

### Other HTTP 500 errors

The API uses status 500 both for its own problems and for requests it
considers invalid. The text after "The API said:" usually says which, for
example "radius must be 50 or less". The package checks its arguments before
sending, so these should be rare. If one says something about your input that
the package let through, please report it.

### HTTP 429 or 503

The API is busy or briefly unavailable. The package waits and retries up to
three times in total. If it still fails, wait a few minutes and try again.

### Errors that mention a timeout or a failed connection

The request didn't reach the API, or got no answer within 30 seconds. Check
your internet connection; if it's working, the API may be down.

## Errors about your arguments

These come from the package, before anything is sent.

| Message | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `` `zipcode` must be a string, such as "02110" `` | You passed a number. Numbers drop leading zeros, so ZIP codes must be strings. |
| `` `zipcode` must be a five-digit ZIP code `` | The string isn't exactly five digits. ZIP+4 codes such as `"02110-1234"` aren't accepted; use the first five digits. |
| `` `radius` must be a whole number `` | Use 1, 2, ... 50, not 2.5. |
| `` `radius` must be between 1 and 50 miles `` | The API's limit is 50 miles. |
| `` `latitude` must be between -90 and 90 `` | Check that latitude and longitude aren't swapped. |
| `` `longitude` must be between -180 and 180 `` | Places in the US have negative longitudes. |
| "Invalid CDC Locator service enum(s)" | A `services` value isn't one of the 14 names. The message lists them. |
| `` `services` must name at least one service `` | You passed an empty vector. Use `services = NULL` for every service. |
| "must be a single non-empty string" | `city` or `state` is missing, blank or has more than one value. |

## Results that look wrong

### No rows

There may be no provider of that kind within the radius. Try a larger radius,
up to 50 miles, or more services. A zero-row result still has all the
columns, so code that uses them keeps working.

### The same clinic appears several times

A clinic that offers several services can have a separate record, with a
different `id`, for each. `vignette("working-with-results")` shows how to keep
one row per place.

### Searching every service gives fewer results than expected

Make sure you're on a version of the package that searches three services at
a time. Asking the API for all 14 at once returns nothing. Any version with
`vignette("services-and-searching")` does this.

### A search is slow

The default search makes five requests, spaced at least half a second apart,
and each takes as long as the API needs to answer. Naming only the services
you need makes fewer requests.

### Results differ from the website

The website at locator.hiv.gov shows some categories the API doesn't offer,
such as tuberculosis testing, and may use newer listings. Listings also change
over time, so results from different days can differ.

## Reporting a problem

If something here doesn't explain what you see, please open an issue at
<https://github.com/VagishHemmige/CDCLocator/issues>. Include the function call,
the full error message and the date. Never include your client ID or token:
the package keeps them out of its messages, so a copied error is safe to share.
